20. Then, he submitted that as the award was already made Rule of the Court and a decree passed following the judgment, no appeal would lie against such decree except on the ground that it was in access of, or not otherwise in 'accordance with, the award and the appellant failed to make out any case within such limited scope. 

 43. It is true a decree was drawn and signed but we could not understand when the award was not made Rule of the Court how a decree could follow such judgment. Be that as it may, the present appeal is preferred against that part of the judgment that rejected the application of the appellant for setting aside the inward. This appeal cannot be termed to be an appeal against the decree. So, the submission of Mr Shafique Ahmed on the scope of the appeal as one against the decree passed under section 17 of the Arbitration Act is wholly misconceived.
